source.title: Questioning Representational Optimism in Deep Learning: The Fractured Entangled Representation Hypothesis
source.authors: Akarsh Kumar; Jeff Clune; Joel Lehman; Kenneth O. Stanley

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses superposition and polysemanticity as related to its Fractured Entangled Representation hypothesis, but its experiments do not test the sparse-feature superposition claims or the listed versions.
record.gate_note: The paper's own experiments compare internal activation maps and weight-sweep effects in Picbreeder-evolved and SGD-trained CPPNs. These bear on the related FER/UFR construct, not on whether sparse features overlap in limited dimensions, SAE features are canonical, or superposition features are one-dimensional. The LLM examples are discussed as suggestive of FER, not as measurements of the listed superposition versions.
record.test_reason: A position paper comparing Picbreeder-evolved and SGD-trained CPPNs on single-image tasks. Its evidence is qualitative: activation-map visualizations, weight sweeps, a PCA basis and random-direction sweeps. It never measures features versus dimensions, sparsity, interference geometry, polysemanticity rates, SAE features or feature dimensionality. Superposition appears in one paragraph of Section 5.1, where the authors say superposition and polysemanticity are 'likely consequences' of fractured, entangled circuitry. That is discussion, not a test. The LLM prompt anecdotes are behavioral and do not touch representation geometry.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors argue that conventional single-objective SGD, in their CPPN experiments, produced fractured entangled representations despite matching outputs. Picbreeder's open-ended evolution produced near-unified factored ones. They speculate that this matters for generalization, creativity and continual learning in large models. They explicitly say not all SGD must yield FER. They describe superposition and polysemanticity as likely consequences of FER without testing this.
record.recipe_differences: The paper compares NEAT-evolved CPPNs with SGD-trained CPPNs on image reproduction, then inspects activation maps and weight-sweep behavior. It does not use the Toy Models of Superposition method or measure feature interference, sparsity, or superposition geometry.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports different results for evolved versus SGD-trained representations and for standard CPPNs versus ReLU-only architectures; PCA gives slightly improved organization relative to the vanilla SGD basis.

fits_no_version.finding: Sweeps along random directions of weight-matrix columns, which do not depend on basis choice, are reported to preserve symmetry and meaningful variation in the Picbreeder CPPN but give meaningless distortions in the SGD CPPN (Appendix F, Fig. 25). The record has no row for this.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In these CPPN examples, the difference in representational organization between evolved and SGD networks persists under basis-agnostic random-direction weight perturbations.

record.problems: The representational comparisons are qualitative and use toy CPPN image tasks. The paper gives no quantitative measure of FER or uncertainty estimates. It states that selected weight sweeps were chosen to show both methods in their best light while remaining broadly representative. Its LLM examples are limited demonstrations and do not measure superposition.
record.rows_left_out: No results directly testing the listed superposition versions were available to record. The paper's LLM behavior examples and its SGD training-trajectory figures were not entered as rows because they do not measure the listed feature-capacity or superposition properties.

untested.parts: All parts: sparse features exceeding dimensions, nearly orthogonal overlapping directions, sparsity-dependent transition, regular geometry.
All parts: whether polysemanticity reflects capacity competition, and whether important features get dedicated dimensions.
All parts. The paper speculates that entanglement comes from the training path, but it does not measure polysemantic neurons or separate the cause from capacity pressure.
All parts: no measurement of LLM neuron distribution of features and no dictionary or SAE recovery.
All parts: no SAE features are examined.
All parts: no analysis of feature dimensionality.

record.verdict_notes: The record's relation (discusses) and tranche (T6) are confirmed, and all rows correctly carry versions ['none']. Two side points for researchers: Figure 25's caption says butterfly while the Appendix F text describes skull sweeps, and the selected sweeps were chosen to show each method 'in their best light' (all sweeps are at the code link). Neither affects the superposition verdict.

versions.untested_parts: Sparse features, feature-to-dimension ratios, overlapping directions, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular superposition geometry.
Whether polysemanticity results from competition for representational capacity, or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
Whether polysemantic neurons arise for reasons other than capacity pressure.
Whether LLM features spread across neurons or sparse features are recoverable with a dictionary or SAE.
Whether SAE features are complete, stable, canonical units of model representation.
Whether superposed features are one-dimensional directions rather than multidimensional features.

rows.subject: Picbreeder Skull CPPN
rows.operation_detail: Visualized neuron activation maps layer by layer.
rows.measure: Organization and reuse in internal activation maps
rows.value: The representation is described as organized: symmetry emerges early, and key features appear once and influence the skull as a whole.
rows.note: Evidence about UFR, not a measurement of superposed sparse features.

rows.subject: Conventional SGD CPPN
rows.operation_detail: Visualized neuron activation maps layer by layer.
rows.measure: Organization and reuse in internal activation maps
rows.baseline: Picbreeder Skull CPPN, which the paper describes as organized and symmetric early in the network
rows.value: The representation is described as disorganized and patchwork; the two sides do not appear symmetric until the output layer, with more novel patterns than necessary.
rows.note: The output behavior matches the target image, but this is not a test of superposition geometry.

rows.subject: Picbreeder Butterfly CPPN
rows.measure: Organization and symmetry in internal activation maps
rows.value: The representation is described as well organized, with y-axis symmetry emerging early and aspects of the output specified once.
rows.note: A result about UFR, not sparse-feature overlap.

rows.subject: Conventional SGD CPPN
rows.measure: Organization and symmetry in internal activation maps
rows.baseline: Picbreeder Butterfly CPPN, described as organized and symmetric early in the network
rows.value: The representation is described as less organized, with left and right wings encoded separately and high-frequency patterns stitched together.
rows.note: The paper interprets this as FER; it does not test superposition.

rows.subject: Picbreeder Apple CPPN
rows.measure: Organization and decomposition in internal activation maps
rows.value: The stem and body are described as encoded separately early in the network and later combined; the representation has a small number of genuinely novel feature maps.
rows.note: A result about modularity and UFR, not the listed superposition versions.

rows.subject: Conventional SGD CPPN
rows.measure: Organization and decomposition in internal activation maps
rows.baseline: Picbreeder Apple CPPN, described as separately representing stem and body
rows.value: The representation is described as fragmented and entangled, without clear separation of apple, stem, and background.
rows.note: The paper interprets this as FER, not as superposition.

rows.subject: Picbreeder Skull CPPN
rows.operation_detail: Swept individual network weights and observed output changes.
rows.measure: Semantic coherence and modularity of output changes under weight sweeps
rows.value: The selected sweeps produce meaningful changes, including controls for mouth opening, eye winking, eye width, and jaw width.
rows.note: The authors state the selected sweeps were chosen to present both methods in their best light while remaining broadly representative.

rows.subject: Conventional SGD CPPN
rows.operation_detail: Swept individual network weights and observed output changes.
rows.measure: Semantic coherence and modularity of output changes under weight sweeps
rows.baseline: Picbreeder Skull CPPN, whose selected sweeps produce meaningful semantic changes
rows.value: The sweeps are described as producing meaningless distortions; the paper says all SGD weights lead to similarly meaningless perturbations.
rows.note: The paper reports selected sweeps and says they are broadly representative; no quantitative score is reported.

rows.subject: Picbreeder Butterfly CPPN
rows.operation_detail: Swept individual network weights and observed output changes.
rows.measure: Semantic coherence and symmetry of output changes under weight sweeps
rows.value: The sweeps are described as producing human-recognizable changes that respect y-axis symmetry, including changes to wing area, color, and vertical shape.
rows.note: A result about UFR and adaptability, not superposition.

rows.subject: Conventional SGD CPPN
rows.operation_detail: Swept individual network weights and observed output changes.
rows.measure: Semantic coherence and symmetry of output changes under weight sweeps
rows.baseline: Picbreeder Butterfly CPPN, whose sweeps are described as meaningful and symmetry-preserving
rows.value: The sweeps are described as deleterious changes that often break symmetry.

rows.subject: Picbreeder Apple CPPN
rows.operation_detail: Swept individual network weights and observed output changes.
rows.measure: Semantic coherence and modularity of output changes under weight sweeps
rows.value: Some weights are described as independently controlling apple size, stem angle, background, or stem removal.
rows.note: A result about modularity, not the capacity or geometry in the claim versions.

rows.subject: Conventional SGD CPPN
rows.operation_detail: Swept individual network weights and observed output changes.
rows.measure: Semantic coherence and modularity of output changes under weight sweeps
rows.baseline: Picbreeder Apple CPPN, whose sweeps can control aspects independently
rows.value: The sweeps are described as often entangling multiple concepts; even similar size controls also change other parts, such as the stem.

rows.subject: Conventional SGD CPPN (ReLU architecture)
rows.value: The maps are described as showing skull shapes with erratic high-frequency artifacts that cancel at the output.
rows.note: This result concerns FER in the paper's sense, not listed superposition versions.

rows.subject: Conventional SGD CPPN (ReLU architecture)
rows.measure: Organization and symmetry of internal activation maps
rows.value: The maps are described as containing numerous asymmetric and disorganized intermediate patterns.
rows.note: The authors say these visualizations still exhibit FER.

rows.subject: Conventional SGD CPPN (ReLU architecture)
rows.value: The maps are described as lacking organization or structured decomposition.
rows.note: The authors say these visualizations still exhibit FER.

rows.subject: Conventional SGD CPPN
rows.operation_detail: Projected layer feature data onto principal components and visualized the resulting feature dimensions.
rows.measure: Organization of internal representation in a transformed feature basis
rows.value: The PCA visualization shows slightly improved organization but remains far from the Picbreeder UFR visualization.
rows.note: This is not an analysis of superposition feature directions.
rows.check: The link is correct. 'Partial' here describes how far PCA reorganizes the SGD representation relative to the vanilla basis, a FER measure. It does not bear on any superposition version.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
